mainTopic: שופר: intent in blowing and hearing, the order and length of the blasts, and their sources in the פסוקים
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: one clause of a ברייתא about children blowing שופר speaks of a קטן who has reached חינוך, and the other speaks of a younger child. The גמרא then draws two inferences from the משנה's rule about a מתעסק. The first seems to support רבא, who says one who blows for music fulfills the מצוה. The second seems to refute רבי זירא, who required the blower to have the listener in mind. Both times the גמרא shows the משנה's wording may not carry the inference. A new משנה follows. It teaches the order of the blasts (three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה) and their lengths. It also covers the case of a שופר that becomes available only after the ברכות, and the מחלוקת over whether the שליח ציבור can fulfill the obligation for everyone. In the גמרא, אביי reconciles a ברייתא about the length of a תקיעה with the משנה. He then admits a real מחלוקת about whether a תרועה is made of שברים or יבבות, based on the crying of סיסרא's mother. Finally, a ברייתא derives from the יובל פסוקים that the blasts must be done with a שופר, with a plain blast before and after each תרועה. It applies all of this to ראש השנה through the words 'בחדש השביעי'.

steps.title: Two clauses, two ages of child
steps.stepSummary: The clash between the two clauses of the ברייתא is resolved. One clause speaks of a קטן who has reached חינוך, and the other speaks of a קטן who has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [There, the ברייתא is speaking] about a child who has reached the age of training. Here, it is about a child who has not reached the age of training.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a contradiction from the previous section. The two statements about children blowing שופר are talking about children of different ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One clause said we actively work with children until they learn to blow. The other said we merely don't stop them. A child old enough for חינוך is actively taught, so that clause is about him. A younger child is simply not prevented, so that clause is about him.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child not yet obligated in מצוות
Reached the age of training in מצוות
Here, meaning in this case or clause

steps.whatToRemember: A child who has reached חינוך is actively taught to blow שופר. A younger child is simply not stopped from blowing.

phrases.english: [There it refers] to a minor who has reached the age of training;
phrases.notes: The word 'כאן' (there) that opens this answer appears just before this amud begins.

phrases.english: here it refers to a minor who has not reached the age of training.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: each clause is assigned to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses seemed to give opposite instructions about the same child.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two clauses speak of children of different ages, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and drawing an inference about music
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a מתעסק does not fulfill the מצוה. It infers that someone who blows for music does fulfill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who is just fiddling [with the שופר] has not fulfilled [the מצוה].' This implies that one who blows for music has fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and reads an implication into it. This is a setup for the next step, where the inference will be used as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is someone who isn't even trying to produce a proper blast. The משנה excludes only him. So someone who deliberately blows a real sound, just for music and not for the מצוה, seems to be included as fulfilling.

keyTerms.meaning: One acting unawares or fiddling, with no intent to produce the proper sound
Has not fulfilled his obligation
This implies, introducing an inference from the wording
One who blows the שופר for music, not for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the מתעסק with the תוקע לשיר. The מתעסק doesn't intend to make a proper blast at all. The תוקע לשיר intends the blast, just not as a מצוה.

phrases.english: And one who acts unawares has not fulfilled [his obligation].
This implies: one who blows for music has fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה rules that a מתעסק does not fulfill the מצוה, and the inference is that a תוקע לשיר does.

steps.title: Does the משנה support רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the inference from the משנה supports רבא, who rules that a תוקע לשיר fulfills the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבא? For רבא said: One who blows for music has fulfilled [the מצוה].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the inference from the משנה backs up the ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that blowing for music still counts, which suggests one need not have intent for the מצוה itself. The inference from the משנה matches his view exactly, so it looks like a source for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a proposed proof or challenge
Supports him
רבא, an אמורא of the fourth generation in בבל

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rava?
For Rava said:
One who blows for music has fulfilled [his obligation].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 2 as a proof
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a תוקע לשיר fulfills the מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the משנה's statement that only a מתעסק fails

steps.title: Blowing for music may also count as fiddling
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The term מתעסק in the משנה may also include someone who blows for music.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps one who blows for music is also called a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבא by reading the word מתעסק more broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the משנה's category of מתעסק is narrow. If the משנה uses that word for anyone blowing without intent for the מצוה, the musician is also excluded. Then the משנה could even argue with רבא. The proof falls, though רבא's view is not disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. It introduces a rejection by offering another reading
Calls him, meaning he is labeled as

steps.whatToRemember: No proof for רבא from the משנה. The word מתעסק might include one who blows for music.

phrases.english: Perhaps one who blows for music
is also called 'one who acts unawares.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא תּוֹקֵעַ לָשִׁיר נָמֵי מִתְעַסֵּק קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed מתעסק is narrow. It may include the תוקע לשיר.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the listener and drawing an inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one who hears from a מתעסק has not fulfilled the מצוה. It infers that one who hears from someone blowing for himself has fulfilled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who hears from a מתעסק has not fulfilled.' But one who hears from someone blowing for himself, what is the law? He has fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה and draws another inference. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only rules out hearing from a מתעסק. So hearing from a person who blows properly but only for his own מצוה seems acceptable. That would mean the blower does not need to have the listener in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hears
One who sounds the שופר for himself only, without intending to fulfill the מצוה for others
What [is the law]?

phrases.english: And one who hears from one who acts unawares has not fulfilled [his obligation].

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִן הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לְעַצְמוֹ, מַאי?
phrases.english: But one who hears from one who sounds for himself, what [is the law]?
He has fulfilled [his obligation].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִן הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ לְעַצְמוֹ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel move to step 2, on the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה rules that hearing from a מתעסק does not count. The inference is that hearing from one blowing for himself does count.

steps.title: A challenge to רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: The inference seems to refute רבי זירא. He told his attendant to have him in mind while blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי זירא? For רבי זירא said to his attendant: 'Have intent [for me] and blow for me!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inference from step 5 to challenge רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא insisted that the blower intend the blowing on his behalf. This implies the listener does not fulfill the מצוה without that intent. The משנה's inference says the opposite, that hearing someone blow for himself is enough. So רבי זירא's view looks refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be a refutation of him
רבי זירא, an אמורא who moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל
His attendant
Have intent

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Zeira?
For Rabbi Zeira said to his attendant:
Have intent and blow for me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 5 to attack רבי זירא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's requirement that the blower intend the blowing for the listener
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that hearing from one blowing for himself counts. That means the blower's intent for the listener is unnecessary, which contradicts רבי זירא.

steps.title: The second clause just copies the first clause's wording
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. The משנה used מתעסק in the second clause only because it had used it in the first, so no inference can be drawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, since the first clause taught about a מתעסק, the second clause also taught about a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. It says the משנה's wording in the second clause was chosen for style, not to teach anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 5 depended on the משנה choosing the word מתעסק on purpose. The גמרא says the second clause simply follows the wording of the first clause. So the משנה is silent about someone blowing for himself, and רבי זירא is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of. It introduces a stylistic explanation
The first clause
The latter clause
Taught, meaning stated in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Neither inference from the משנה holds up. There is no proof for רבא and no refutation of רבי זירא, because the משנה's word מתעסק may be broad or merely stylistic.
steps.whyThisMatters: The איידי argument is a common tool across ש״ס. A word may appear only to match the parallel clause, so no inference can be drawn from it.

phrases.english: Perhaps, since the first clause taught 'one who acts unawares,'
the latter clause also taught 'one who acts unawares.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the סיפא, so the משנה no longer refutes רבי זירא (though it does not prove him right either)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge treated the word מתעסק in the סיפא as chosen on purpose. It is really just a copy of the רישא's wording.

steps.title: The order of the blasts and how long each one is
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that there are three sets of three blasts each. A תקיעה equals three תרועות in length, and a תרועה equals three יבבות. One long blast cannot count as two separate תקיעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The order of the blasts is three sets of three blasts each. The length of a תקיעה is like three תרועות. The length of a תרועה is like three short whimpering sounds. Suppose someone blew the first תקיעה, then stretched out the second תקיעה (the one closing the set) to the length of two, hoping it would count twice. He gets credit for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out the basic structure of the שופר blasts and how long each blast must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each set is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and it is done three times, giving nine blasts in all. The last תקיעה of one set and the first תקיעה of the next set must be two separate blasts. Stretching one long blast does not combine them into two.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the שופר blasts
A long, straight, steady blast
A broken, wavering blast made of short sounds
Short whimpering or sobbing sounds
The required length or measure
He has only one to his credit

phrases.english: MISHNA: The order of the blasts:
three sets of three blasts each.
phrases.notes: Each set is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.

phrases.english: The length of a tekia is like three teruot,
the length of a terua is like three whimpers.
If he blew the first [tekia],
and stretched out the second tekia to the length of two,
phrases.notes: He wanted this one long blast to serve as the end of the first set and the start of the second set.

phrases.english: he has only one in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic after the discussion of מתעסק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. A תקיעה equals three תרועות, and a תרועה equals three יבבות. One stretched-out blast cannot count as two תקיעות.

steps.title: Someone who got a שופר only after saying the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: Someone said the ברכות of מוסף, and only afterward did a שופר become available. He still blows all three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said the ברכות, and only afterward did a שופר become available to him. He blows תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches what to do if the שופר arrives late, after the person has already finished the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the blasts are blown during the ברכות of מוסף (מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות). If he missed that chance, the מצוה of שופר is not lost. He blows the full nine blasts in a row.

keyTerms.meaning: Who said the ברכות (here, the ברכות of מוסף)
A שופר became available to him
Blows a תרועה

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבירך refers to the ברכות of מוסף on ראש השנה. It does not mean the ברכה said right before blowing שופר.

phrases.english: One who recited the blessings
and afterward a shofar became available to him —
he blows a tekia, a terua, and a tekia, three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבֵּירַךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַנָּה לוֹ שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with a new case about the blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שופר arrives after the ברכות, he still blows all three sets in a row.

steps.title: Does each person have to daven, or does the prayer leader cover everyone?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says every individual is obligated in the ראש השנה תפילה, just like the שליח ציבור. רבן גמליאל says the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the שליח ציבור is obligated, so too every single individual is obligated. רבן גמליאל says: the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת. The question is whether each person must daven the long ראש השנה תפילה himself, or whether he can rely on the prayer leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that the שליח ציבור's תפילה does not replace each person's own obligation. רבן גמליאל holds that listening to the שליח ציבור counts as fulfilling the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader who davens for the congregation
An individual
Fulfills the obligation on their behalf
The תנא who disagrees and lets the שליח ציבור cover everyone

steps.confusionAlert: This מחלוקת is about the ברכות of תפילה, not about the שופר blasts themselves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a question that comes up throughout שס: whether a שליח ציבור can fulfill the obligation of תפילה for others.

phrases.english: Just as the prayer leader is obligated,
so too each and every individual is obligated.
Rabban Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: The prayer leader fulfills the obligation on behalf of the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final clause of the same משנה, about the ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says every individual is obligated. רבן גמליאל says the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a different length for a תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a תקיעה is as long as one תרועה, not as long as three.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But it was taught in a ברייתא: the length of a תקיעה is like a תרועה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out a contradiction. A ברייתא gives a shorter length for a תקיעה than the משנה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a תקיעה equals three תרועות. The ברייתא says it equals one תרועה. Both cannot be true as written.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
Like one תרועה

phrases.english: GEMARA: But it was taught in a baraita:
The length of a tekia is like a terua!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the משנה's measurement in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a תקיעה equals three תרועות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a תקיעה equals only one תרועה, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: אביי: the two sources count differently
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה counts the תקיעות and תרועות of all three sets together. The ברייתא counts only one set. So the two sources agree: one תקיעה equals one תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Our תנא counts the תקיעה of all the sets and the תרועות of all the sets. The ברייתא's תנא counts just one set and no more.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He shows that the two sources are measuring the same thing in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every set has one תרועה, so across three sets there are three תרועות. The משנה means that all the תקיעות of one kind across the three sets equal the three תרועות together. On a per-set basis, that is one תקיעה per one תרועה, which is exactly what the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of our משנה
The תנא of the ברייתא (the outside teaching)
He is counting
Sets / one set
And no more

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a תקיעה is as long as one תרועה. The משנה's three תרועות refers to all three sets added together.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The tanna of our mishna counts
the tekia of all the sets
and the teruot of all the sets.
The tanna of the baraita counts
one set and no more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי תַּנָּא דִּידַן קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciling two sources by showing they count differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require a תקיעה three times as long as a תרועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts all three sets together, while the ברייתא counts one set. So one תקיעה equals one תרועה.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts the length of a תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a תרועה is as long as three יבבות, then challenges it with a ברייתא that says a תרועה is as long as three שברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the length of a תרועה is like three whimpers. But a ברייתא teaches: the length of a תרועה is like three broken blasts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It immediately raises a ברייתא that seems to give a different length for the תרועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures a תרועה by short whimpering sounds (יבבות). The ברייתא measures it by longer broken sounds (שברים). Three שברים take longer than three יבבות, so the two sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Measurement or length
Short whimpering blasts
Broken blasts, longer than whimpers
'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' This opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different challenge from step 11. Step 11 was about how long a תקיעה is. This one is about what a תרועה is made of: יבבות or שברים.

phrases.english: The length of a teruah is like three whimpers.
But it was taught: the length of a teruah is like three broken blasts!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (for the quote of the משנה)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the length of the תקיעה was settled in step 12, the גמרא turns to the משנה's next measurement, the תרועה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a תרועה equals three יבבות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines the תרועה as three שברים, which is a different and longer sound than three יבבות.

steps.title: אביי: here the תנאים truly disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי admits that this ברייתא really disagrees with the משנה. He shows that both sides agree a תרועה is a crying sound, based on the תרגום and the crying of סיסרא's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: on this point they certainly disagree. The Torah says 'It shall be a day of תרועה for you,' and the Aramaic translation says 'It shall be a day of יבבא for you.' And about the mother of סיסרא it is written: 'Through the window she looked out, and the mother of סיסרא cried (ותיבב).'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not try to make the sources agree this time. He says this is a real מחלוקת, and he starts showing where the disagreement comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום shows that the Torah's word תרועה means יבבא, a crying sound. The פסוק about סיסרא's mother uses the same word for her crying. Both sides accept this. The question that remains is what kind of crying she did, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly disagree
And we translate it (in the Aramaic תרגום)
Crying or wailing sound
The mother of סיסרא, who cried at the window waiting for her son (שופטים ה)

steps.confusionAlert: In step 12 אביי made the sources agree. Here he does the opposite. He says the ברייתא and the משנה really do argue.

phrases.english: Abaye said: in this they certainly disagree,
as it is written: 'It shall be a day of teruah for you,'
and we translate: 'It shall be a day of yevava for you.'
And it is written about the mother of Sisera:
'Through the window she looked out,'
'and the mother of Sisera wailed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by saying the two sources truly disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admitting a real מחלוקת between תנאים, and tracing it back to a shared source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא and the משנה must agree, the way אביי made the sources agree in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: They really disagree. Both treat a תרועה as crying, but they understand the crying differently.

steps.title: Moaning versus whimpering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא holds that סיסרא's mother moaned with long sighs (שברים). The משנה holds that she whimpered with short sobs (יבבות).
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage thinks she moaned with long sighs. The other Sage thinks she whimpered with short cries.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now names the exact point of the מחלוקת. It is about what kind of crying the word ויבב describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גנוחי means long, broken groans, like the שברים. ילולי means short, rapid whimpers, like the יבבות. The ברייתא follows the first view and the משנה follows the second.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds
She moaned with long sighs (like שברים)
She whimpered with short sobs (like יבבות)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a תרועה is a crying sound. They argue about whether it is long moaning (שברים) or short whimpering (יבבות).
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is the source of the practical doubt about the תרועה sound. That doubt is why we blow both שברים and תרועה today.

phrases.english: One Sage holds she groaned with moans.
And one Sage holds she wailed with whimpers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer by stating each side's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא (three שברים) reads the crying as moaning. The משנה (three יבבות) reads it as whimpering.

steps.title: Where do we learn the blasts must be with a שופר
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא asks for the source that the required blasts are done with a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: from where do we know that the blasts are done with a שופר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. This question sets up the source given in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of ראש השנה only says 'a day of תרועה.' It does not say which instrument to use. The ברייתא wants a source that it must be a שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
From where do we know?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: from where do we know that it is with a shofar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the length of the תרועה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the תרועה must be blown with a שופר

steps.title: The source: the יובל verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with the פסוק 'והעברת שופר תרועה,' which says the יובל blasts are done with a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall sound the שופר of תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a פסוק that clearly mentions a שופר. That פסוק is talking about יום כיפור of the יובל year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Torah directly connects the word תרועה with a שופר. That is the clear source for using a שופר. But it only covers the יובל, so the next step asks about ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
'You shall sound the שופר of תרועה' (ויקרא כה:ט)

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And you shall sound the shofar of teruah.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:ט, about יום כיפור of the יובל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יובל פסוק explicitly requires a שופר for the תרועה.

steps.title: What about ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the פסוק only covers the יובל, and asks how we know the same rule for ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only teaches me about the יובל. From where do we know it for ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap in its own source. This sets up a second derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about יום כיפור of the יובל year, not about ראש השנה. So we still need a way to apply the שופר requirement to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from this source)
The fiftieth (Jubilee) year, announced with a שופר on יום כיפור

phrases.english: I have only the Jubilee;
for Rosh Hashanah, from where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 17 is limited to the יובל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that ראש השנה also requires a שופר

steps.title: 'בחדש השביעי' links all the seventh-month blasts
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בחדש השביעי' are not needed, because the פסוק already says יום הכפורים. So they teach that all the blasts of the seventh month must be alike, and ראש השנה also needs a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'in the seventh month.' The Torah did not need to say 'in the seventh month,' so why does it say it? To teach that all the תרועות of the seventh month must be like one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds an extra phrase in the פסוק and uses it to stretch the שופר rule to ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows יום כיפור falls in the seventh month, so the words 'בחדש השביעי' seem extra. The extra words teach that all the blasts of תשרי follow one pattern. Since the יובל blast on יום כיפור is with a שופר, the ראש השנה blast in the same month must be with a שופר too.

keyTerms.meaning: In the seventh month (תשרי)
Since the פסוק did not need to say it
This one like that one, alike

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש השנה שופר is learned from the יובל שופר. The extra words 'בחדש השביעי' make all the blasts of תשרי alike.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison (all seventh-month blasts are alike) is used again later to learn more details about the ראש השנה blasts from the יובל.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'In the seventh month.'
Since there was no need for the verse to say 'in the seventh month,'
what does the verse teach by saying 'in the seventh month'?
That all the teruot
of the seventh month should be like one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by using the extra words in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra phrase 'בחדש השביעי' makes all seventh-month blasts alike, so ראש השנה also requires a שופר.

steps.title: Where do we learn a plain blast comes before the תרועה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that a straight blast (פשוטה) must come before the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that a plain, straight blast comes before it (the תרועה)?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא already showed that we need a תרועה. Now it asks a new question to set up the next answer: how do we know a straight blast comes first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תרועה is a broken, wavering sound. The ברייתא wants a source for a plain, unbroken blast (a תקיעה) placed right before it. This is the first half of the pattern תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: A straight, plain, unbroken blast (a תקיעה)
Before it, meaning before the תרועה
A broken, wavering שופר sound
The standard name for the straight blast

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'פשוטה' does not mean 'simple' in the sense of 'easy'. It means 'straight', which is the plain blast we call a תקיעה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes before it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing the שופר and the תרועה, the ברייתא now asks about the blast that comes before the תרועה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק source showing that a plain blast must come before each תרועה.

steps.title: The word 'שופר' before 'תרועה' teaches a plain blast first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from 'והעברת שופר תרועה'. The word שופר comes before the word תרועה, so a plain שופר blast comes before the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall sound a שופר blast, a תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by reading the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'שופר' first and only then 'תרועה'. The ברייתא reads this order as an order of sounds. A plain שופר sound (a פשוטה) comes first, and then the תרועה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a verse as the source)
And you shall sound or pass around (the שופר)
A ram's horn; here it stands for a plain blast of the horn

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Then you shall sound the shofar, a terua.'
phrases.notes: 'Shofar' comes before 'terua', so a straight blast comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the word שופר comes before תרועה in the פסוק, a plain blast must come before the תרועה.

steps.title: Where do we learn a plain blast comes after the תרועה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that a straight blast must also come after the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that a plain, straight blast comes after it (the תרועה)?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא asks the matching question about the end of the set, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 only covered a blast before the תרועה. The ברייתא now looks for a source for a closing plain blast. With that blast the full pattern would be תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: After it, meaning after the תרועה
And from where (do we know this)?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a straight blast comes after it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 20 and asks about the blast after the תרועה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק source showing that a plain blast must follow each תרועה.

steps.title: 'תעבירו שופר' teaches a plain blast after the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: Later in the same פסוק it says 'תעבירו שופר' again. This second mention of the שופר comes after the תרועה, so it teaches a plain blast after the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'You shall sound the שופר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by pointing to a second, later mention of the שופר in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק reads: 'והעברת שופר תרועה... ביום הכפורים תעבירו שופר'. The second 'שופר' comes after the word תרועה. So it teaches a plain blast after the תרועה, and this completes the set: plain blast, תרועה, plain blast.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural) shall sound or pass around
The day in the יובל year when these blasts are sounded

steps.whatToRemember: Every תרועה has a plain תקיעה before it (from 'שופר תרועה') and a plain תקיעה after it (from 'תעבירו שופר').

phrases.english: The verse states: 'You shall sound the shofar.'
phrases.notes: This second mention of the שופר comes after the תרועה, so it teaches the blast that comes after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'שופר', which comes after the תרועה in the פסוק, requires a plain blast after the תרועה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the basic shofar set we blow: תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה.

steps.title: Does the before-and-after rule also apply on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that these פסוקים only speak about the יובל. It asks how we know the same before-and-after pattern on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for the יובל. From where do we know it for ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits what it just learned to the יובל and asks how to extend it to ראש השנה. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the words it used ('שופר תרועה', 'תעבירו שופר') come from the פסוק about יום הכפורים of the יובל year. So on their own they teach only about the יובל. The ברייתא needs a link that carries the pattern over to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from this source) about…
The fiftieth year, announced with the שופר on יום הכפורים
The New Year, the first day of the seventh month

phrases.english: I have derived this only for the Jubilee Year;
from where do we know it on Rosh HaShana?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹבֵל, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same move as step 18, now for the before-and-after blasts instead of the use of a שופר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that applies the plain blasts before and after the תרועה to ראש השנה.

steps.title: 'בחדש השביעי' carries the pattern over to ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with 'בחדש השביעי'. These words link all the blasts of the seventh month, so ראש השנה also has a plain blast before and after each תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'In the seventh month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the final answer: the words 'בחדש השביעי' apply the יובל pattern to ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As in step 19, the words 'בחדש השביעי' are extra, because the פסוק already says יום הכפורים. They teach that all the blasts of the seventh month are alike. ראש השנה is also in the seventh month, so it gets the same תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: In the seventh month (תשרי)
Extra words in a פסוק that are used to teach something new

steps.whatToRemember: On ראש השנה, just like the יובל, every תרועה is surrounded by a plain blast before and after. We learn this from the words 'בחדש השביעי'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why on ראש השנה each set of blasts starts and ends with a תקיעה.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'In the seventh month.'
phrases.notes: These words link all the blasts of the seventh month, so ראש השנה follows the יובל pattern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 with the same kind of link used in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'בחדש השביעי' make all the blasts of the seventh month alike, so ראש השנה also needs a plain blast before and after each תרועה.
